definitions.explanation: Having no equal or rival. Used to emphasize that something or someone is in a class of their own, with nothing comparable.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{無類|むるい}の{読書|どくしょ}{好|ず}きだ。
examples.english: He is an unparalleled lover of reading.

examples.japanese: {無類|むるい}の{強|つよ}さを{誇|ほこ}るチームだ。
examples.english: A team that boasts unmatched strength.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{無類|むるい}の{酒|さけ}{好|ず}きで、{毎晩|まいばん}{日本酒|にほんしゅ}を{飲|の}んでいた。
examples.english: My grandfather was an incomparable sake lover and drank nihonshu every night.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{無類|むるい}の{美|うつく}しさを{持|も}つ{自然|しぜん}に{恵|めぐ}まれている。
examples.english: This region is blessed with nature of incomparable beauty.

notes:
Used almost exclusively in the pattern {無類|むるい}の + noun to mean "an unparalleled (something)." The most common usage by far is {無類|むるい}の〜{好|ず}き, describing someone who is an extreme enthusiast of something.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無類|むるい}の{酒|さけ}{好|ず}き: an incomparable sake lover
- {無類|むるい}の{読書|どくしょ}{好|ず}き: an unparalleled book lover
- {無類|むるい}の{強|つよ}さ: unmatched strength
- {無類|むるい}の{美|うつく}しさ: incomparable beauty

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {無比|むひ}: unequaled — very similar meaning, slightly more literary
- {比類|ひるい}ない: without peer — more formal, often in written prose
- {唯一|ゆいいつ}{無二|むに}: one and only — emphasizes uniqueness rather than superiority
- {天下|てんか}{無双|むそう}: peerless under heaven — dramatic, used in historical or literary contexts

FORMATION:
{無|む} (without) + {類|るい} (category, kind) — literally "without category," meaning nothing of the same kind exists.
